claims.statement: For every finite ordinary connected tree T with integer p=alpha(T)-2 and first strict descent x(T), eligibility x(T)+2<=p implies alpha(T)>=7.
claims.scope: Exactly ordinary finite connected trees, strict zero-extended Delta ranks, and the frozen alpha-minus-two eligibility condition; proof composes r27 n<=4x with elementary tree identities and the n=7,8 vertex-cover cases.
claims.reason: The assumption alpha<=6 forces alpha=6, x=2, n in {7,8}; exact tree counting and the corresponding one- or two-vertex-cover bounds force Delta_2>0, contradicting Delta_x<0. No eligible alpha<=6 tree or defect in these steps was found.

claims.statement: The displayed 9-vertex tree has alpha=7, x=3, p=5, is eligible, has six favorable original leaves, and complete sum S=-56.
claims.scope: One self-built finite ordinary tree, independently enumerated over all subsets by the included standalone script; no census or universal sign claim.
claims.reason: The script computes the independent-set sequence, first strict descent, every original-leaf selector and term, and the exact complete favorable sum from the explicitly listed edges.

limitations: No attack on the alpha>=7 eligibility claim or its cited r27 and small-tree steps was found; the result is proposed and does not alter canonical status.
The fresh order-nine replay is one exact graph only; no new exhaustive census or Lean build was run.
This work does not prove the tagged bipartite shadow bound, the high-tail leaf pointwise sign, or the primary complete-sum theorem, all of which remain unresolved here.
No owned background jobs remain running.
